| `github.com/containerd/stargz-snapshotter/estargz` | `v0.18.2` -> `v0.19.0`                               |

It is missing c/storage. I am not sure if it is a problem. PTAL @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers

Yes, that switches to an older stable branch, and reverts various fixes. Please manually update c/storage to the same digest (and after https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1239, Go should no longer downgrade to 1.64.2 again).

### Edited/Blocked Notification

Renovate will not automatically rebase this PR, because it does not recognize the last commit author and assumes somebody else may have edited the PR.

You can manually request rebase by checking the rebase/retry box above.

 ⚠️ **Warning**: custom changes will be lost.

At some point we really should file a but to renovate about this. The go tooling clearly works fine without our branching/merge back git logic. I do not get why renovate fails to simply pick of the latest commit on main when we do that merge. It is rather annoying.
On Buildah, it worked without any issues. https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/pull/7174

Yes, because Buildah was already at 1.64.3-0.…. Podman was at 1.64.2-0.…, so the release 1.64.2 was seen as an upgrade.

AFAICT this is a Go behavior, Renovate is ~innocent. Sure it could be programmed so that commit references to `main` are always updated to later commit references to `main`, and not to tags on a branch, but any other external consumer would still prefer the tag on a branch.

> AFAICT this is a Go behavior, Renovate is ~innocent. Sure it could be programmed so that commit references to main are always updated to later commit references to main, and not to tags on a branch, but any other external consumer would still prefer the tag on a branch.

Well yes go get does the wrong thing because go does not know what branching strategies are.
Yet renovate is not innocent either IMO
```
WARN: Package lookup failures
{
  "warnings": [
    "Could not determine new digest for update (go package go.podman.io/storage)"
  ],
  "files": [
    "go.mod"
  ]
}
```

That is not helpful either. If it would indeed just follow what go does it should have cleanly update storage as well.
As can be seen by the PR it did not consider storage at all, the 1.64.2 switch was just a indirect dep due common and image.

For example see here https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/pull/6940 for when we just did common. In that case common gets ignored forever until we manually update it past the merge point or to a tag which is clearly not normal
And yes I updated buildah past the merge point here last week https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/pull/7169 so it is happy.
Oh, I did not notice that Renovate error. Thanks.
